statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the ACK control bit is set, this field contains the value of the next sequence number the sender of the segment is expecting to receive. Once a connection is established, this is always sent.
statements.guard_semantics: connection.state = ESTABLISHED

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN: 1 bit -- Synchronize sequence numbers.
statements.guard_semantics: connection.state = SYN-SENT | connection.state = SYN-RECEIVED

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN: 1 bit -- No more data from sender.
statements.guard_semantics: connection.state = FIN-WAIT-1 | connection.state = LAST-ACK | connection.state = CLOSING

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: RST: 1 bit -- Reset the connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If SYN is set, the sequence number is the initial sequence number (ISN) and the first data octet is ISN+1.
statements.guard_semantics: segment.SYN = 1

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: RST: 1 bit -- Reset the connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSED - represents no connection state at all. CLOSED is fictional because it represents the state when there is no TCB, and therefore, no connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LISTEN - represents waiting for a connection request from any remote TCP peer and port.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-SENT - represents waiting for a matching connection request after having sent a connection request.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-RECEIVED - represents waiting for a confirming connection request acknowledgment after having both received and sent a connection request.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: ESTABLISHED - represents an open connection, data received can be delivered to the user. The normal state for the data transfer phase of the connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-1 - represents waiting for a connection termination request from the remote TCP peer, or an acknowledgment of the connection termination request previously sent.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-2 - represents waiting for a connection termination request from the remote TCP peer.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSE-WAIT - represents waiting for a connection termination request from the local user.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSING - represents waiting for a connection termination request acknowledgment from the remote TCP peer.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LAST-ACK - represents waiting for an acknowledgment of the connection termination request previously sent to the remote TCP peer (this termination request sent to the remote TCP peer already included an acknowledgment of the termination request sent from the remote TCP peer).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TIME-WAIT - represents waiting for enough time to pass to be sure the remote TCP peer received the acknowledgment of its connection termination request and to avoid new connections being impacted by delayed segments from previous connections.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The OPEN call specifies whether connection establishment is to be actively pursued, or to be passively waited for. A passive OPEN request means that the process wants to accept incoming connection requests, in contrast to an active OPEN attempting to initiate a connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SND.UNA = oldest unacknowledged sequence number

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SND.NXT = next sequence number to be sent

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: RCV.NXT = next sequence number expected on an incoming segment, and is the left or lower edge of the receive window

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: RCV.NXT+RCV.WND-1 = last sequence number expected on an incoming segment, and is the right or upper edge of the receive window

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A new acknowledgment (called an 'acceptable ack') is one for which the inequality below holds: SND.UNA < SEG.ACK =< SND.NXT
statements.guard_semantics: SND.UNA < SEG.ACK & SEG.ACK =< SND.NXT

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Segment acceptability test (Table 5): SEG.LEN=0 & RCV.WND=0 → SEG.SEQ=RCV.NXT; SEG.LEN=0 & RCV.WND>0 → RCV.NXT=<SEG.SEQ<RCV.NXT+RCV.WND; SEG.LEN>0 & RCV.WND=0 → not acceptable; SEG.LEN>0 & RCV.WND>0 → RCV.NXT=<SEG.SEQ<RCV.NXT+RCV.WND or RCV.NXT=<SEG.SEQ+SEG.LEN-1<RCV.NXT+RCV.WND
statements.guard_semantics: (SEG.LEN = 0 & RCV.WND = 0 & SEG.SEQ = RCV.NXT) | (SEG.LEN = 0 & RCV.WND > 0 & RCV.NXT =< SEG.SEQ & SEG.SEQ < RCV.NXT+RCV.WND) | (SEG.LEN > 0 & RCV.WND > 0 & ((RCV.NXT =< SEG.SEQ & SEG.SEQ < RCV.NXT+RCV.WND) | (RCV.NXT =< SEG.SEQ+SEG.LEN-1 & SEG.SEQ+SEG.LEN-1 < RCV.NXT+RCV.WND)))

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A TCP receiver MUST process the RST and URG fields of all incoming segments, even when the receive window is zero (MUST-66).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: the TIME-WAIT state limits the rate of connection reuse, protecting against ambiguity about which incarnation of a connection an incoming packet corresponds to

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Step 1 of three-way handshake: A --> B SYN my sequence number is X

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Steps 2 and 3 of three-way handshake (combined): A <-- B ACK your sequence number is X / SYN my sequence number is Y
actions: send ACK of sequence number X

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Step 4 of three-way handshake: A --> B ACK your sequence number is Y; completes connection establishment
actions: send ACK of sequence number Y

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: For a connection to be established or initialized, the two TCP peers must synchronize on each other's initial sequence numbers via an exchange of segments carrying the SYN control bit
statements.guard_semantics: must be set during three-way handshake to synchronize ISNs

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: the TCP endpoint must keep quiet for an MSL before assigning any sequence numbers upon starting up or recovering from a situation where memory of sequence numbers in use was lost
statements.trigger: startup or recovery from sequence number memory loss

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: if a TCP endpoint is reinitialized in some sense, yet retains its memory of sequence numbers in use, then it need not wait at all; it must only be sure to use sequence numbers larger than those recently used
statements.trigger: reinitialization with retained sequence number memory
actions: use sequence numbers larger than those recently used

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: For this specification the MSL is taken to be 2 minutes

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Hosts that for any reason lose knowledge of the last sequence numbers transmitted on each active (i.e., not closed) connection shall delay emitting any TCP segments for at least the agreed MSL in the internet system that the host is a part of.
statements.trigger: loss of sequence number knowledge on active connection
actions: delay emitting any TCP segments for at least MSL seconds

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: One way to deal with this problem is to deliberately delay emitting segments for one MSL after recovery from a reboot -- this is the 'quiet time' specification.
actions: delay emitting TCP segments for one MSL after recovery from reboot

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Hosts that for any reason lose knowledge of the last sequence numbers transmitted on each active (i.e., not closed) connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Upon the host rebooting, a TCP peer might re-form an earlier connection (possibly after half-open connection resolution) and emit packets with sequence numbers identical to or overlapping with packets still in the network. The TCP specification recommends that the source delay for MSL seconds before emitting segments on the connection, to allow time for segments from the earlier connection incarnation to drain from the system.
statements.trigger: new connection incarnation after reboot without sequence number memory
actions: delay MSL seconds before emitting segments on the connection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSED: no connection exists; used as the starting state before a connection is initiated.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LISTEN: TCP peer is waiting for a connection request from any remote TCP peer.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-SENT: TCP peer has sent a SYN segment and is awaiting a matching connection response; a non-synchronized state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-RECEIVED: TCP peer has received a SYN and sent a SYN-ACK, awaiting final ACK; a non-synchronized state. TCP implementation must track whether this state was reached via passive OPEN or active OPEN.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: ESTABLISHED: connection is fully synchronized; data transfer is possible. Data buffered at the receiver until this state is reached.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-1: a synchronized closing state; RST causes connection abort and user notification.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-2: a synchronized closing state; RST causes connection abort and user notification.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSE-WAIT: a synchronized closing state; RST causes connection abort and user notification.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSING: a synchronized closing state; RST causes connection abort and user notification.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LAST-ACK: a synchronized closing state; RST causes connection abort and user notification.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TIME-WAIT: a synchronized closing state; RST causes connection abort and user notification.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Non-synchronized states are SYN-SENT and SYN-RECEIVED; a TCP peer in these states returns to LISTEN on receiving an acceptable reset.
statements.guard_semantics: receive acceptable RST -> return to LISTEN

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Synchronized states are ESTABLISHED, FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSE-WAIT, CLOSING, LAST-ACK, TIME-WAIT; a TCP peer in these states aborts the connection and informs its user on receiving a RST.
statements.guard_semantics: receive RST -> abort connection & inform user

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A TCP implementation MUST keep track of whether a connection has reached SYN-RECEIVED state as the result of a passive OPEN or an active OPEN (MUST-11).
statements.guard_semantics: protocol.state = SYN-RECEIVED

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 6, line 2: TCP Peer A sends a SYN segment, transitioning from CLOSED to SYN-SENT.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 6, line 2: TCP Peer B receives a SYN segment, transitioning from LISTEN to SYN-RECEIVED.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 6, line 3: TCP Peer A receives SYN,ACK, transitioning from SYN-SENT to ESTABLISHED, then sends ACK.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 6, line 4: TCP Peer B receives the final ACK, transitioning from SYN-RECEIVED to ESTABLISHED.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 7: During simultaneous open, each TCP peer in SYN-SENT receives a SYN (without ACK) and transitions to SYN-RECEIVED. Each TCP peer's connection state cycles from CLOSED to SYN-SENT to SYN-RECEIVED to ESTABLISHED.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 7: During simultaneous open, each TCP peer in SYN-RECEIVED receives SYN,ACK and transitions to ESTABLISHED.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the receiving TCP peer is in non-synchronized state SYN-SENT, it returns to LISTEN on receiving an acceptable reset.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the receiving TCP peer is in non-synchronized state SYN-RECEIVED, it returns to LISTEN on receiving an acceptable reset.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the TCP peer is in one of the synchronized states (ESTABLISHED, FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSE-WAIT, CLOSING, LAST-ACK, TIME-WAIT), it aborts the connection and informs its user on receiving a RST.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = ESTABLISHED | protocol.state = FIN-WAIT-1 | protocol.state = FIN-WAIT-2 | protocol.state = CLOSE-WAIT | protocol.state = CLOSING | protocol.state = LAST-ACK | protocol.state = TIME-WAIT

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TCP Peer A is in CLOSED state after reboot; no connection exists at its end.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TCP Peer B is in ESTABLISHED state, believing the connection is open (send 300, receive 100).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TCP Peer A is in SYN-SENT state after sending SYN to reopen the connection following a reboot.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Two TCP Peers A and B with passive connections waiting for SYN are both in LISTEN state (Figure 11).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TCP Peer B moves to SYN-RECEIVED state when an old duplicate SYN arrives while in LISTEN (Figure 11, line 2).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: After TCP Peer A reboots (causing loss of memory), it starts in CLOSED state (Figure 9, line 2).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: After TCP Peer A reboots, the user attempts to reopen the connection; A's TCP implementation sends a segment containing SYN, transitioning from CLOSED to SYN-SENT (Figure 9, lines 2-3).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: TCP Peer B, being in a synchronized state (ESTABLISHED) and the incoming SYN segment outside the window, responds with an ACK indicating what sequence it next expects to hear (Figure 9, lines 3-4).
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = ESTABLISHED & segment.SYN_flag = true & segment.sequence_number outside receive_window

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: TCP Peer A sees that the received ACK segment does not acknowledge anything it sent and, being unsynchronized, sends a RST because it has detected a half-open connection; A remains in SYN-SENT (Figure 9, lines 4-5).
statements.trigger: receive ACK (does not acknowledge sent data)
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = SYN-SENT & segment.ACK_flag = true & segment.ACK_num not_in sent_data_range

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: TCP Peer B aborts at line 5 after receiving RST from TCP Peer A, transitioning from ESTABLISHED to CLOSED (Figure 9, lines 5-6).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: In Figure 10, data arriving at TCP Peer A from TCP Peer B is unacceptable because no such connection exists, so TCP Peer A sends a RST.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The RST is acceptable so TCP Peer B processes it and aborts the connection, transitioning from ESTABLISHED to CLOSED (Figure 10, line 3).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An old duplicate SYN arriving at TCP Peer B (LISTEN) stirs B into action, causing B to transition to SYN-RECEIVED and return a SYN-ACK (Figure 11, lines 2-3).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: TCP Peer A, in LISTEN state, receives a SYN-ACK from TCP Peer B where the ACK is not acceptable, causing TCP Peer A to generate a RST while remaining in LISTEN (Figure 11, lines 3-5).
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = LISTEN & segment.SYN_flag = true & segment.ACK_flag = true & segment.ACK_num not_acceptable

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: TCP Peer B accepts the RST and returns to its passive LISTEN state from SYN-RECEIVED (Figure 11, lines 4-5).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The side of a connection issuing a reset should enter the TIME-WAIT state, as this generally helps to reduce the load on busy servers.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the connection does not exist (CLOSED), then a reset is sent in response to any incoming segment except another reset. The connection remains in the CLOSED state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the connection is in any non-synchronized state (LISTEN, SYN-SENT, SYN-RECEIVED), and the incoming segment acknowledges something not yet sent (unacceptable ACK), or has a mismatched security level or compartment, a reset is sent. The connection remains in the same state.
statements.pre_cond: (protocol.state = LISTEN | protocol.state = SYN-SENT | protocol.state = SYN-RECEIVED) & (segment.ACK = unacceptable | segment.security != connection.security)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the connection is in a synchronized state (ESTABLISHED, FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSE-WAIT, CLOSING, LAST-ACK, TIME-WAIT), any unacceptable segment must be responded to with an empty acknowledgment segment containing the current send sequence number and the next sequence number expected to be received, and the connection remains in the same state.
statements.from_state: ESTABLISHED | FIN-WAIT-1 | FIN-WAIT-2 | CLOSE-WAIT | CLOSING | LAST-ACK | TIME-WAIT
statements.pre_cond: (protocol.state = ESTABLISHED | protocol.state = FIN-WAIT-1 | protocol.state = FIN-WAIT-2 | protocol.state = CLOSE-WAIT | protocol.state = CLOSING | protocol.state = LAST-ACK | protocol.state = TIME-WAIT) & segment.unacceptable = 1
actions: send empty ACK with current SND.NXT and RCV.NXT

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the connection is in a synchronized state (ESTABLISHED, FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSE-WAIT, CLOSING, LAST-ACK, TIME-WAIT) and an incoming segment has a security level or compartment that does not exactly match the level and compartment requested for the connection, a reset is sent and the connection goes to the CLOSED state.
statements.from_state: ESTABLISHED | FIN-WAIT-1 | FIN-WAIT-2 | CLOSE-WAIT | CLOSING | LAST-ACK | TIME-WAIT
statements.pre_cond: (protocol.state = ESTABLISHED | protocol.state = FIN-WAIT-1 | protocol.state = FIN-WAIT-2 | protocol.state = CLOSE-WAIT | protocol.state = CLOSING | protocol.state = LAST-ACK | protocol.state = TIME-WAIT) & segment.security != connection.security
actions: send RST with SEQ from incoming segment ACK field

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In all states except SYN-SENT, all reset (RST) segments are validated by checking their SEQ fields. A reset is valid if its sequence number is in the window.
statements.guard_semantics: RST is valid only if SEQ is within the receive window; applies in all states except SYN-SENT

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the SYN-SENT state (a RST received in response to an initial SYN), the RST is acceptable if the ACK field acknowledges the SYN.
statements.guard_semantics: RST is valid in SYN-SENT only if ACK field acknowledges the SYN

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the receiver was in the LISTEN state, it ignores it.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the receiver was in SYN-RECEIVED state and had previously been in the LISTEN state, then the receiver returns to the LISTEN state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the receiver was in SYN-RECEIVED state and had not previously been in the LISTEN state, the receiver aborts the connection and goes to the CLOSED state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the receiver was in any other state, it aborts the connection and advises the user and goes to the CLOSED state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: ESTABLISHED state: the starting point for the normal close sequence (Figure 12, Figure 13).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-1 state: TCP implementation enters this state after the local user initiates CLOSE and a FIN segment is placed on the outgoing segment queue. No further SENDs from the user will be accepted by the TCP implementation. RECEIVEs are allowed in this state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-2 state: reached after the local FIN has been acknowledged by the remote peer (Figure 12, step 3).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSE-WAIT state: entered by the receiving TCP endpoint after receiving an unsolicited FIN from the network and acknowledging it; the user has not yet closed (Figure 12, step 2).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LAST-ACK state: entered after the local user CLOSEs from CLOSE-WAIT and the TCP endpoint sends its own FIN; awaiting final ACK (Figure 12, step 4).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TIME-WAIT state: entered after sending ACK for the remote FIN; the endpoint waits 2 MSL before the connection is deleted (Figure 12, step 5-6; Figure 13, step 4).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSED state: the connection is deleted after completing the normal close handshake or after an abort (Figure 12, step 5-6; Figure 13, step 4).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSING state: entered during simultaneous close when a FIN is received from the remote peer while the local endpoint is in FIN-WAIT-1 (Figure 13, step 3).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Case 1 / Figure 12 step 2: Local user initiates close. A FIN segment can be constructed and placed on the outgoing segment queue. No further SENDs from the user will be accepted by the TCP implementation, and it enters the FIN-WAIT-1 state.
actions: place FIN on outgoing segment queue

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 12 step 2: TCP Peer B transitions from ESTABLISHED to CLOSE-WAIT upon receiving FIN from the remote peer, acknowledging it.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 12 step 3: TCP Peer A transitions from FIN-WAIT-1 to FIN-WAIT-2 upon receiving ACK of its FIN from the remote peer.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 12 step 4 / Case 2: TCP Peer B transitions from CLOSE-WAIT to LAST-ACK upon local user CLOSE, sending a FIN after any remaining data.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 12 step 4: TCP Peer A transitions from FIN-WAIT-2 to TIME-WAIT upon receiving FIN from remote peer, sending ACK.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 12 step 5: TCP Peer B transitions from LAST-ACK to CLOSED upon receiving the final ACK, deleting the connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 12 step 6 / Figure 13 step 4: TCP endpoint transitions from TIME-WAIT to CLOSED after the 2 MSL timer expires.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 13 step 2-3: During simultaneous close, each peer in FIN-WAIT-1 transitions to CLOSING upon receiving the remote FIN, acknowledging it.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Figure 13 step 3-4: During simultaneous close, each peer transitions from CLOSING to TIME-WAIT upon receiving ACK of its FIN.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Case 2: If an ACK is not forthcoming, after the user timeout the connection is aborted and the user is told.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A TCP connection may terminate via an abort in which one or more RST segments are sent and the connection state is immediately discarded.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the local TCP connection is closed by the remote side due to an RST received from the remote side, the connection state is immediately discarded.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When a connection is closed actively, it MUST linger in the TIME-WAIT state for a time 2xMSL (Maximum Segment Lifetime).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When a connection is closed actively, it MUST linger in the TIME-WAIT state for a time 2xMSL (Maximum Segment Lifetime) (MUST-13).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: It MAY accept a new SYN from the remote TCP endpoint to reopen the connection directly from TIME-WAIT state (MAY-2), if it assigns its initial sequence number for the new connection to be larger than the largest sequence number it used on the previous connection incarnation.
statements.trigger: receive new SYN from remote TCP endpoint
actions: assign new ISN larger than previous max sequence number

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Returns to TIME-WAIT state if the SYN turns out to be an old duplicate.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If such a host issues a CLOSE call while received data is still pending in the TCP connection, or if new data is received after CLOSE is called, its TCP implementation SHOULD send a RST to show that data was lost (SHLD-3).
statements.trigger: CLOSE called with pending received data | data received after CLOSE

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: TCP implementations SHOULD send an MSS Option in every SYN segment when its receive MSS differs from the default 536 for IPv4 or 1220 for IPv6 (SHLD-5), and MAY send it always (MAY-3).
actions: include MSS Option in SYN segment

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If an MSS Option is not received at connection setup, TCP implementations MUST assume a default send MSS of 536 (576 - 40) for IPv4 or 1220 (1280 - 60) for IPv6 (MUST-15).
statements.trigger: connection setup completed without MSS Option received
actions: set SendMSS to default (536 for IPv4 or 1220 for IPv6)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TCP endpoints MUST implement both sending and receiving the MSS Option (MUST-14).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Once the connection is established, data is communicated by the exchange of segments.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Note that, once in the ESTABLISHED state, all segments must carry current acknowledgment information.
statements.guard_semantics: protocol.state = ESTABLISHED

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: When the sender creates a segment and transmits it, the sender advances SND.NXT.
actions: advance SND.NXT by segment data and flag length

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: When the receiver accepts a segment, it advances RCV.NXT and sends an acknowledgment.
actions: advance RCV.NXT by segment data and flag length

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: When the data sender receives an acknowledgment, it advances SND.UNA.
actions: advance SND.UNA to acknowledged sequence number

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The CLOSE user call implies a push function (see Section 3.9.1), as does the FIN control flag in an incoming segment.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When the number of transmissions of the same segment reaches a threshold R2 greater than R1, close the connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: An attempt to open a TCP connection could fail with excessive retransmissions of the SYN segment; SYN retransmissions MUST be handled in the general way just described for data retransmissions, including notification of the application layer.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: An attempt to open a TCP connection could fail with excessive retransmissions of the SYN segment or by receipt of a RST segment or an ICMP Port Unreachable.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: An attempt to open a TCP connection could fail with excessive retransmissions of the SYN segment or by receipt of a RST segment or an ICMP Port Unreachable.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: R2 for a SYN segment MUST be set large enough to provide retransmission of the segment for at least 3 minutes (MUST-23).
statements.guard_semantics: Minimum value of R2 for SYN segments; controls when connection open attempt is aborted

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A TCP connection is said to be 'idle' if for some long amount of time there have been no incoming segments received and there is no new or unacknowledged data to be sent.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The application MUST be able to turn keep-alives on or off for each TCP connection (MUST-24), and they MUST default to off (MUST-25).

statements.description: LAST-ACK STATE — listed for processing of sequence number check, RST check, security check, SYN check, ACK check, and FIN bit check

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TIME-WAIT STATE — listed for processing of sequence number check, RST check, security check, SYN check, ACK check, and FIN bit check

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSED state — target state reached after RST processing, security violation, or FIN acknowledgment; TCB is deleted upon entry

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LISTEN state — referenced as target state when a passive-open SYN-RECEIVED connection receives RST or SYN

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-RECEIVED STATE, RST bit set, passive OPEN (came from LISTEN state): return this connection to LISTEN state and return. The user need not be informed. The retransmission queue should be flushed.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-RECEIVED STATE, RST bit set, active OPEN (came from SYN-SENT state): the connection was refused; signal the user 'connection refused', flush retransmission queue, enter CLOSED state, delete TCB.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: ESTABLISHED STATE, RST bit set: any outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND should receive 'reset' responses. All segment queues should be flushed. Users should receive an unsolicited general 'connection reset' signal. Enter the CLOSED state, delete the TCB, and return.
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-1 STATE, RST bit set: any outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND should receive 'reset' responses. All segment queues should be flushed. Users should receive unsolicited 'connection reset' signal. Enter the CLOSED state, delete the TCB.
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-2 STATE, RST bit set: any outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND should receive 'reset' responses. All segment queues should be flushed. Users should receive unsolicited 'connection reset' signal. Enter the CLOSED state, delete the TCB.
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSE-WAIT STATE, RST bit set: any outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND should receive 'reset' responses. All segment queues should be flushed. Users should receive unsolicited 'connection reset' signal. Enter the CLOSED state, delete the TCB.
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSING STATE, RST bit set: enter the CLOSED state, delete the TCB, and return.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LAST-ACK STATE, RST bit set: enter the CLOSED state, delete the TCB, and return.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TIME-WAIT STATE, RST bit set: enter the CLOSED state, delete the TCB, and return.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-RECEIVED STATE, security check: if the security/compartment in the segment does not exactly match the security/compartment in the TCB, then send a reset and return.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: ESTABLISHED STATE, security check: if security/compartment does not match TCB, send reset, outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND receive 'reset' responses, flush all segment queues, signal 'connection reset', enter CLOSED state, delete TCB.
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-1 STATE, security check: if security/compartment does not match TCB, send reset, outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND receive 'reset' responses, flush all segment queues, signal 'connection reset', enter CLOSED state, delete TCB.
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-2 STATE, security check: if security/compartment does not match TCB, send reset, outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND receive 'reset' responses, flush all segment queues, signal 'connection reset', enter CLOSED state, delete TCB.
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSE-WAIT STATE, security check: if security/compartment does not match TCB, send reset, outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND receive 'reset' responses, flush all segment queues, signal 'connection reset', enter CLOSED state, delete TCB.
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSING STATE, security check: if security/compartment does not match TCB, send reset, outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND receive 'reset' responses, flush all segment queues, signal 'connection reset', enter CLOSED state, delete TCB.
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LAST-ACK STATE, security check: if security/compartment does not match TCB, send reset, outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND receive 'reset' responses, flush all segment queues, signal 'connection reset', enter CLOSED state, delete TCB.
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TIME-WAIT STATE, security check: if security/compartment does not match TCB, send reset, outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND receive 'reset' responses, flush all segment queues, signal 'connection reset', enter CLOSED state, delete TCB.
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-RECEIVED STATE, SYN bit set, passive OPEN: if the connection was initiated with a passive OPEN, then return this connection to the LISTEN state and return.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Synchronized states (ESTABLISHED, FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSE-WAIT, CLOSING, LAST-ACK, TIME-WAIT), SYN bit set, SYN is in the window (non-RFC 5961 behavior): send a reset, outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND receive 'reset' responses, flush all segment queues, signal 'connection reset', enter CLOSED state, delete TCB. Representative entry for ESTABLISHED.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = ESTABLISHED & segment.SYN = 1 & RCV.NXT <= SEG.SEQ & SEG.SEQ < (RCV.NXT + RCV.WND)
actions: send 'reset' response to outstanding RECEIVEs and SEND

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-RECEIVED STATE, ACK bit on, SND.UNA < SEG.ACK =< SND.NXT: enter ESTABLISHED state and continue processing with SND.WND <- SEG.WND, SND.WL1 <- SEG.SEQ, SND.WL2 <- SEG.ACK.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = SYN-RECEIVED & segment.ACK = 1 & SND.UNA < SEG.ACK & SEG.ACK <= SND.NXT
statements.post_cond: protocol.state = ESTABLISHED & SND.WND = SEG.WND & SND.WL1 = SEG.SEQ & SND.WL2 = SEG.ACK

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-1 STATE, ACK bit on: in addition to the processing for the ESTABLISHED state, if the FIN segment is now acknowledged, then enter FIN-WAIT-2 and continue processing in that state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSING STATE, ACK bit on: in addition to the processing for the ESTABLISHED state, if the ACK acknowledges our FIN, then enter the TIME-WAIT state; otherwise, ignore the segment.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LAST-ACK STATE, ACK bit on: the only thing that can arrive in this state is an acknowledgment of our FIN. If our FIN is now acknowledged, delete the TCB, enter the CLOSED state, and return.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TIME-WAIT STATE, ACK bit on: the only thing that can arrive in this state is a retransmission of the remote FIN. Acknowledge it, and restart the 2 MSL timeout.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Do not process the FIN if the state is CLOSED, LISTEN, or SYN-SENT since the SEG.SEQ cannot be validated; drop the segment and return.
statements.guard_semantics: FIN bit may only be processed when protocol.state != CLOSED & protocol.state != LISTEN & protocol.state != SYN-SENT

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-RECEIVED STATE, FIN bit set: signal user 'connection closing', return pending RECEIVEs with same message, advance RCV.NXT over FIN, send ACK for FIN. Enter the CLOSE-WAIT state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: ESTABLISHED STATE, FIN bit set: signal user 'connection closing', return pending RECEIVEs with same message, advance RCV.NXT over FIN, send ACK for FIN. Enter the CLOSE-WAIT state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-1 STATE, FIN bit set, our FIN has been ACKed (perhaps in this segment): enter TIME-WAIT, start the time-wait timer, turn off the other timers.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-1 STATE, FIN bit set, our FIN has NOT been ACKed: enter the CLOSING state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: FIN-WAIT-2 STATE, FIN bit set: enter the TIME-WAIT state. Start the time-wait timer, turn off the other timers.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSE-WAIT STATE, FIN bit set: remain in the CLOSE-WAIT state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: CLOSING STATE, FIN bit set: remain in the CLOSING state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LAST-ACK STATE, FIN bit set: remain in the LAST-ACK state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TIME-WAIT STATE, FIN bit set: remain in the TIME-WAIT state. Restart the 2 MSL time-wait timeout.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: For any state if the user timeout expires, flush all queues, signal the user 'error: connection aborted due to user timeout' in general and for any outstanding calls, delete the TCB, enter the CLOSED state, and return.
actions: signal user error: connection aborted due to user timeout

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: For any state if the retransmission timeout expires on a segment in the retransmission queue, send the segment at the front of the retransmission queue again, reinitialize the retransmission timer, and return.
actions: send segment at front of retransmission queue

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the time-wait timeout expires on a connection, delete the TCB, enter the CLOSED state, and return.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Enter the CLOSED state after user timeout or time-wait timeout expires and TCB is deleted.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TIME-WAIT state in which the time-wait timeout may expire, causing the connection to enter CLOSED.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TCB: Transmission control block, the data structure that records the state of a connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: RST: A control bit (reset), occupying no sequence space, indicating that the receiver should delete the connection without further interaction. The receiver can determine, based on the sequence number and acknowledgment fields of the incoming segment, whether it should honor the reset command or ignore it. In no case does receipt of a segment containing RST give rise to a RST in response.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: MSL: Maximum Segment Lifetime, the time a TCP segment can exist in the internetwork system. Arbitrarily defined to be 2 minutes.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-RECEIVED remembers last state (MUST-11)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In TIME-WAIT state for 2MSL seconds (MUST-13)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Function: simultaneously LISTENs for same port (MUST-42)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: SYN-RECEIVED remembers last state (MUST-11): the connection must retain which prior state was active when transitioning into SYN-RECEIVED

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Accept SYN from TIME-WAIT state (MAY-2)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Close connection on R2 retransmissions (MUST-20)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Inform application of aborted conn (MUST-12): TCP must inform the application layer when a connection is aborted

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Support simultaneous open attempts (MUST-10)
